title: Untwisted scalar and restriction comparison of resolution sections
statement: Let f:X→T be a scheme morphism [def-pc-morphism-conventions], F an O_X-module with an injective resolution I, q a natural number, W an open of T and a a section of O_T on W. Define K=f_*I and P(V)=H^q(K(V)) by [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-open-choices]. Let Y=f inverse W, G=F restricted to Y, b the pullback of a to Γ(Y,O_Y), and s=b times the standard generator of the tensor unit, with nonvanishing locus as in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. There is an additive equivalence c:P(W)≃H^q(Y,G), using [def-sc-open-module-cohomology], such that for every open U of Y equal to the nonvanishing locus of s there is an additive equivalence d:P(D(a))≃H^q(U,G) commuting with restriction. For every natural n and x in P(W), H^q(Y,smulHom(G,b^n))(c(x))=c(a^n x). There are no tensor powers of G in these equivalences.

lean.statement:
theorem resolution_open_scalar_comparison {X T : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ T) (F : X.Modules) (I : InjectiveResolution F) (q : ℕ)
    (W : T.Opens) (a : Γ(T, W)) :
    let K := ((pushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex
    let P := sectionCohomologyPresheaf K q
    let Y := (f ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme
    let G := (restrictFunctor (f ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι).obj F
    let b := ((f.app W) ≫ (f ⁻¹ᵁ W).topIso.inv).hom a
    let s : Γ(𝟙_ Y.Modules, ⊤) := unitSectionsEquiv ⊤ b
    ∃ c : P.obj (op W) ≃+
        (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology Y.toRingedSpace q ⊤).obj G,
      (∀ (U : Y.Opens), (U : Set Y) = nonvanishingLocus (𝟙_ Y.Modules) s →
        ∃ d : P.obj (op (T.basicOpen a)) ≃+
          (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology Y.toRingedSpace q U).obj G,
          ∀ x : P.obj (op W),
            (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomologyRestriction Y.toRingedSpace q
              (homOfLE (le_top : U ≤ ⊤))).app G (c x) =
                d ((P.map (homOfLE (T.basicOpen_le a)).op).hom x)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : P.obj (op W)),
        (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology Y.toRingedSpace q ⊤).map
          (G.smulHom (b ^ n)) (c x) = c (a ^ n • x))
